events.text: Sunbok notices the new knot in your cord and looks away. That evening the tea at Little Mae's place goes unpoured, and she does not come.

effects.log: You explain. Mae hears you out, and says at the end, "I know. I know why." It does not help.
You drink alone. The cord keeps you company.

events.text: Old Man Gal of the Barrows turns the new knot in your cord with a thumb and nods. "Neat work," he says. "That one will feed well."

effects.log: He nods, slightly. In the Barrow Fellowship that is a deep compliment.
You say nothing. He takes it for yes.

events.text: You left that wonhon waiting and it did not wait kindly. A barn burned down, a child slipped off a wall, and the {spt_grade} grudge of {spt_who} has swelled with every season since.

effects.log: You go. It turns to you with something like reproach.

choices.text: Tell the village to keep away

effects.log: They keep away, and talk about you instead.

The village you promised sends a boy on a mule: the {spt_grade} grudge of {spt_who} is walking the fields at dusk, and the reapers will not stay out past noon.

events.text: Three years left alone, and the grudge has soaked into the wells and the walls. Every house in the district dreams of {spt_who}.

choices.text: Vow that it will be this year

effects.log: This year. You scratch it on the shrine wall so you cannot forget.

choices.text: Tell the district to boil its water

effects.log: They boil it and still dream. The grudge does not live in the water. It lives in what was done.

variants: The grudge of {spt_who} has gone into the ground. The district's grain comes up pale, and every hearth in it burns low and cold, whatever is put on it.
Three untended years: families are leaving the district by the cartload. Those who stay hang bells on every door, and the bells ring for {spt_who}.

events.text: You come to in a turnip field, hatless, mud to the knee, with a stranger's lullaby on your tongue. The farm folk say you came knocking at midnight for a husband who died forty years back.

events.text: In the small hours the {spt_grade} wonhon rips itself free of your cord and is gone through the shutters. Dogs bark the length of the lane till light, and the sill is raked with scratches on the inside.

effects.log: You go after it with a bell. It is gone into the hills, and it is angry.
You let it go. The cord is lighter, and you are ashamed of how glad you are.

events.text: Nobody pumps water when you are in the lane any more. Mothers shoo their children indoors and bar the door as you walk by.

events.text: At dusk a girl no taller than the gatepost comes to your door alone. "Folk say you can speak with the dead," she says. "Could you find my mum?"

effects.log: You look. Her mother is at peace, and says to eat her greens. The girl laughs and cries.
You send her home. She goes, looking back.

events.text: A stranger in graveyard grey takes the stool opposite yours at a roadside inn: Old Man Gal of the Barrows. "Three on your cord," he says, "and a heart like a winter well. The shrine will never forgive that. We'd never ask it to."

effects.log: You drink the cup of barrow-water he pours. You are of the Fellowship now.
He finishes his ale and leaves you the reckoning. "We'll be about," he says.

events.text: A coffin lid is left at your door with your name burned into it and an invitation chalked underneath. The Barrow Fellowship meets at the dark of the moon.

choices.text: Go at the dark of the moon

effects.log: You go. The Fellowship stands in a ring among the barrows and makes room for you.
You burn the lid. The smoke smells of old flowers.

events.text: One night you let the wonhon off its cord over a village that had done nobody wrong. It crawls back at dawn, fatter and colder, and the village behind it is far quieter than a village should be.

effects.log: You do not think about it. That is the first lesson of the Fellowship.

choices.text: Go and look at the village

effects.log: You go and look. You wish you had not.

events.text: Exorcist Ma Yeongdo of the Temple of the Peach-Wood Sword is in the district, asking after a keeper of the Barrow Fellowship. Their peach-wood blade is older than you, and they do not smile.

events.text: At dusk they lay you in an open grave, barley heaped on your chest, and all night the bound dead sing above. Come morning the grave is opened and you sit up, your heart slow and cold, a drum heard through a wall.

effects.log: You stand. The dead bow to you. The living take a step back.
You lie and listen to the earth. It knows your name now.

events.text: The earth will not keep you and will not let you go. At noon they dig you out grey and shaking, and for three days you say nothing.

effects.log: Next year. The grave is patient. So are you.
You swear it. The cord on your wrist goes cold, disappointed.

events.text: You ring your bell-cord and the funeral bell at once. The risen watchers by your door turn their faces to the cord, and the cold of the bound dead drains into them like water into dry sand.

effects.log: You watch. One of them stands a little straighter after.
You look away. It is not a thing to watch.
